Associated Keywords: arvow review, ai seo automation, credit based seo tools, autoblogging alternatives
Friction: Arvow bills one credit pool that three different jobs draw from — articles at about 10 credits, AI images at 3 each, site optimization at 1 per page. Every roundup divides the allowance by the article rate alone and reports 100 articles a month on the $99 Solo plan. Add two images per post and the same allowance buys 62; make them long-form and it buys 38. Buyers compare that inflated number against per-article competitors and pick on arithmetic that was never going to hold.
Logic: Price the pool the way you will actually spend it. Solo's 1,000 credits are 100 bare articles, 62 with two images each, or 38 if they run past 18 headings where the article rate doubles — a 2.6x spread inside one advertised number, and the spread widens as your content gets better. Then compare across billing units honestly: Byword sells articles outright at $99 for 25, Outrank a fixed 30-article bundle at $99, RightBlogger unlimited words metered by site at $59, Autoblogging.ai a separate credit meter from $19. Credit pools win on flexibility and lose on predictability; the question is whether you would rather cap your volume or cap your surprise. We are not an alternative: audit-only, no generation.
content_angle: The advertised article count assumes you publish text with no images and never run the site optimizer — three jobs share one credit pool, so the real capacity is 38 to 100 articles depending on how you work. Every figure first-party with a verification date, the credit rules quoted from the vendor's own FAQ, and the vendor's own $129-vs-$149 internal inconsistency noted without inferring a third price. Names our own position: audit-only, no generation.
